subject.title: [Feature]: Allow Gateway-relay Talk clients to declare realtime tools

question: Should Gateway-relay Talk expose client-executed realtime tools through a globally configured `talk.realtime.clientTools` list, or should declarations be supplied and scoped by the owning client/session during session creation?
rationale: Both shapes can reuse the existing relay result path, but they have materially different multi-client, reconnect, capability-discovery, and compatibility semantics; source evidence does not establish an approved permanent contract.

options.title: Use client/session declarations
options.body: Add a typed owner-scoped declaration at session creation so provider-visible tools exactly match the client that can execute them.

options.title: Use global configuration
options.body: Add `talk.realtime.clientTools` only if maintainers intend one operator-defined capability set shared by all eligible relay clients.

options.title: Defer the surface
options.body: Keep the current built-in tool set until an explicit generic client-capability protocol is designed.

recommendation.title: Use client/session declarations
recommendation.body: Add a typed owner-scoped declaration at session creation so provider-visible tools exactly match the client that can execute them.

likelyOwner.reason: The author has supplied the clearest concrete protocol proposal, while current-main history ownership could not be verified in the available read-only environment.
